text:
oncall-bot: PAGER: P1 runtime-serving: multiple pods in gpu-pool are restarting and customers reporting 503s. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/ephemeral-storage-evict. Please ack.

maria: acked. I'm on it, switching my status to paging.

ashok: seeing repeated evictions on node gnf-12: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age                 From                Message
  ----     ------       ----                ----                -------
  Warning  Evicted      3m (x12 over 30m)   kubelet, gnf-12     The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
```
Pod logs show modelcache writing temp snapshots and the logging agent spiking io.

kevin: GPU-serve pods show OOMKilled and then CUDA error on restart: "CUDA error: driver shutting down" in the runtime logs. Looks correlated with node flapping.

sara: customer-success-bot reporting 3 customers on dedicated instances saw request timeouts and degraded throughput. CS triage asked for ETA.

maria: quick impact check: metric stream shows 18% error rate increase for /v1/generate, median latency up ~320ms -> 900ms for affected region. A handful of requests got 500s. Suspect model cache purge + container restarts causing cold-cache latency + backend errors.

ashok: digging into disk usage: ssh'ed into gnf-12, root cause appears to be runaway /var/log/journal and model cache tmp snapshots. du -sh output: 
```
# du -sh /var/log/journal /var/lib/modelcache /tmp
3.2G	/var/log/journal
42G	/var/lib/modelcache
11G	/tmp
```
Modelcache process wrote huge tmp snapshots during a checkpoint loop. Logging agent (filebeat) was also re-trying and buffering to disk when ES was throttled.

kevin: also found kubelet eviction thresholds low on that node: kubelet config had evictionHard: {"ephemeral-storage": "200Mi"} — which is aggressive for model cache nodes.

maria: mitigation plan (short): 1) reduce log verbosity on the modelcache pods, 2) rotate/delete old journal files to free space, 3) cordon and drain one affected node at a time, 4) fallback route traffic to warm model-variants in other region until node pool is healthy.

ashok: executing step 2 now: truncated journal and rotated: 
```
sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M && sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald
rm -rf /var/lib/modelcache/tmp/snap-*  # removing partial snapshots
```
Result: freed ~35GB. Node now shows free ephemeral storage.

deploy-bot: i-rollback:deployed image runtime:v2.14.1 -> runtime:v2.14.0 to reduce aggressive snapshotting (requested by @maria).

kevin: after freeing disk, some pods still failing with CUDA driver errors — looks like GPU dGPU process lost context during repeated container restarts. Suggested action: full pod restart on healthy nodes to reinitialize drivers.

maria: taking node gnf-12 out of rotation: `kubectl cordon gnf-12 && kubectl drain gnf-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` then recreate pods on other nodes.

ashok: started drain, but drain hung on pods using local SSD (modelcache with emptyDir). Worked around by patching deployment to reduce emptyDir size via env var and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=120. Rolling restart to move pods.

sara: CS updated impacted customers: "We’re actively mitigating a storage-related incident affecting ~3 clusters in A region. We have traffic fallbacks in place and expect reduced errors in 30–45 minutes." :thumbsup:

kevin: monitoring: errors dropped from 18% -> 6% after disk freed and partial restarts, but some tail latency still high due to cache cold starts.

maria: action checklist completed for initial mitigation: free disk, cordon+drain, reduce logging, rollback snapshot change, restart affected pods. Next: 1) update kubelet eviction thresholds for GPU pools, 2) add preemptive logrotate for modelcache logs, 3) introduce limit on snapshot size/age in runtime, 4) write an alert for modelcache-temp-growth.

ashok: add note: we observed journald growth because filebeat retry queue filled when ES endpoint responded 429s. Need to throttle or route to S3 buffer.

kevin: customer impact summary for postmortem: 
- Affected customers: 3 dedicated tenants in region A (IDs: tenant-792, tenant-811, tenant-903) reported increased 500s and latency spikes.
- Duration: incident start ~2100123456 -> mitigations reduced errors by 2100126600 (~55 minutes to major improvement).
- Root cause: combined factors: modelcache checkpoint loop writing large tmp files + logging agent buffering -> exhausted ephemeral-storage -> kubelet evicted pods -> container restart churn -> CUDA context loss and runtime OOMs.

maria: handing off to on-call for next shift @kevin. I will write up a short post-incident runbook note.

oncall-bot: Handoff: oncall->kevin. Please ack within 10 minutes.

kevin: acked, I'll own follow-ups. Immediate items assigned to kevin/ashok/maria/sara.

maria: TODOs assigned: 
- kevin: tune kubelet evictionHard to 2Gi for ephemeral-storage on GPU pools + roll config via daemonset.
- ashok: add runtime config that caps modelcache tmp snapshot size and add metric export `modelcache.tmp_bytes`.
- maria: add durable buffer for filebeat (S3 fallback) and reduce ES ingestion spikes.
- sara: follow up with CS on customer reimbursements and update status page.

customer-success-bot: Customer notification sent: "We're investigating and have mitigation in place. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps."

kevin: rolling kubelet config change scheduled (canary 1 node then full rollout). ETA for config rollout 3 hours. I'll also open a postmortem ticket and link metrics/graphs.

maria: collecting logs and attachments for postmortem: kubectl describe pod, kubelet logs, journal size history, du outputs, and modelcache debug snapshots.

ashok: added quick grep for eviction messages across cluster: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep -i ephemeral-storage` — flagged 27 evictions in the past 40m.

kevin: closing: keeping incident thread open until postmortem doc exists. Thanks all for speed. :heart:

maria: note for postmortem: propose follow-ups: increase ephemeral-storage quota for model nodes, adopt persistent modelcache PVC option for large models, and implement runbook automated mitigations (auto rotate journal + auto delete partial snapshots).

sara: logging final customer update scheduled in 2 hours.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Major mitigations completed. Monitoring will remain in watch for 4h.

kevin: last check: error rate back to baseline by 2100127800. Setting status to monitoring.

maria: thanks — filing postmortem doc and linking to this thread.
